content.rationale: A single undifferentiated list of related ids would lose the distinction mkyoyqvt draws and mnovnnot fixes: depends_on and evaluates differ in who is the parent and who is the child, so the same id can be a prerequisite of the selected node or a node it evaluates, and a flat list could be read backwards. Splitting by direction into depends_on and evaluates (the edges the node's own fields declare) and dependents and evaluators (the edges other nodes' fields declare toward it) keeps each id's role unambiguous, and it means the panel shows both what the selected node declares and what names it, which is what a reader walking the graph from that node needs. Naming a section after the edge type for the node's own fields and after the derived direction for the reverse lookup keeps each label tied to one direction rather than to an arrow the reader has to reconstruct. Keeping every section present with a label and an explicit empty state, including the evaluates section that is always empty for a decision, shows the absence of a relation as a fact instead of an omission that looks like a bug or a missing panel. The decision reuses vqwoptmu's labelled-section frame rather than inventing a second presentation, and it deliberately stops at which sections exist and what each one contains: collapse, node-content rendering and the sections' placement relative to kind, content and rationale belong to other decisions, so this node neither restates nor constrains them.
content.content:
The detail panel lists the selected node's relationships as four labelled sections: "depends_on", "evaluates", "dependents" and "evaluators". The four labels and their contents are fixed as follows, and each direction matches mkyoyqvt and mnovnnot: a depends_on edge runs from the listed prerequisite (parent) to the declaring node (child), and an evaluates edge runs from the declaring evaluator (parent) to the listed evaluated node (child).

- The "depends_on" section lists the ids in this node's own depends_on: the prerequisites the selected node lists. By direction each listed id is that prerequisite and the selected node is the declaring child, so this section names the selected node's depends_on parents.
- The "evaluates" section lists the ids in this node's own evaluates: the nodes the selected node names as evaluated. By direction the selected node is the declaring evaluator and each listed id is the evaluated child, so this section names the nodes the selected node evaluates. A decision never carries evaluates, so for a selected decision this section's entry list is empty.
- The "dependents" section lists the nodes whose depends_on names the selected node. By direction the selected node is the parent and each listed node is a depends_on child, so this section names the selected node's dependents.
- The "evaluators" section lists the evaluations whose evaluates names the selected node. By direction each listed evaluation is the evaluator parent and the selected node is the evaluated child, so this section names the evaluations that evaluate the selected node.

The "depends_on" and "evaluates" labels are the selected node's own field names, as in vqwoptmu's labelled sections; "dependents" and "evaluators" are derived labels because no node field carries them. They are not a third and fourth edge type: each is the same depends_on or evaluates edge read from the other end, so the panel still shows exactly the two edge types of mkyoyqvt.

All four sections appear for every selection, each labelled with its fixed label above, whether or not it has entries. A section with no entries still appears with its label and an explicit empty state (text within the labelled section saying it has no entries) rather than being omitted, hidden or rendered blank. Keeping the four sections distinct means a reader can tell whether an id is a prerequisite of the selected node, a node the selected node evaluates, a node that depends on the selected node, or an evaluation that evaluates it; two sections (depends_on and evaluators) name the selected node's parents and two (evaluates and dependents) name its children.

This decision adds these four relationship sections to the labelled-section frame of vqwoptmu and does not change that frame's three sections or their fixed kind, content, rationale order. Whether sections can be collapsed, how each listed id's node content is rendered, and where the relationship sections sit relative to the kind, content and rationale sections are left to other decisions.
